long_biography.plain_text:
In Soviet-era Ukraine, Jan Koum grew up conscious that telephone conversations could be monitored; after emigrating to California at 16, expensive calls home reinforced the value of private, affordable communication. He taught himself computer networking, left university for an infrastructure job at Yahoo and spent nearly nine years learning how dependable services were run.

After buying an iPhone, Koum recognised that the new App Store could transform software distribution. WhatsApp began as a status tool, but Apple's push-notification feature let early users answer one another, exposing its potential as a messenger. Former Yahoo colleague Brian Acton joined him, and the pair kept the product focused: no advertising, no games and minimal user data. That discipline supported unusually fast adoption with a small engineering team.
